title: Buying an Air Conditioner in Australia: The Real Cost Explained

scenes.heading: Air conditioning: compare the real cost

cues.text: Hi, welcome to Smart Choice three sixty five. Today, we are looking at the real cost of buying an air conditioner in Australia.

scenes.heading: Make the comparison easier to see

cues.text: If the video looks blurry, choose ten eighty p in your quality settings. Menus can vary by device.
Subscribe for practical comparisons that help you buy smarter.

scenes.note: Illustrated settings guide; not a clickable control

scenes.heading: The cheapest box is not the full story

cues.text: Our starting point: compare the right-sized system, your climate zone, and the complete installed cost.
A lower purchase price does not tell you which option will cost less over time.

scenes.note: Smart Choice 365 editorial approach · No hands-on product testing

scenes.heading: 1. Start with your room

cues.text: Ask an installer to assess the actual space before choosing a size.
Windows, sun exposure and the building matter. A quick floor-area rule is only a starting point.
Compare systems suitable for that room, rather than assuming a bigger unit is the better buy.

scenes.note: YourHome guidance + our buying checklist · Generic illustrative scene

scenes.heading: 2. Read the right numbers

cues.text: Cooling capacity in kilowatts describes output. It is not a promise of constant electricity consumption.
For a running-cost comparison, look at annual cooling energy in kilowatt hours.
Use the same hot, average or cold climate zone, and keep cooling separate from heating.

scenes.note: Australian Energy Rating guidance · No fabricated product label shown

scenes.heading: 3. Turn annual energy into dollars

cues.text: Here is a teaching example, not two real products or a current electricity offer.
At an assumed thirty cents per kilowatt hour, nine hundred kilowatt hours costs two hundred and seventy dollars a year.
Six hundred kilowatt hours costs one hundred and eighty dollars.
The difference is ninety dollars a year, under those assumptions.

scenes.note: Hypothetical annual cooling figures · A$0.30/kWh assumed · Supply charges excluded

scenes.heading: 4. Is the higher upfront cost worth it?

cues.text: Suppose the more efficient option costs four hundred and fifty dollars more, fully installed.
At ninety dollars annual savings, simple payback is five years.
At forty cents per kilowatt hour, the same energy difference saves one hundred and twenty dollars a year. Payback becomes three point seven five years.
These are illustrative calculations, not guaranteed savings. They exclude finance, repairs and maintenance differences.

scenes.note: Invented comparison · Unchanged usage and rates assumed · Not actual product prices

scenes.heading: 5. Portable does not mean anywhere

cues.text: A portable air conditioner can help when a fixed installation is impractical.
But check where the exhaust hose goes and whether the window kit fits before buying.
Check the exact model's noise and room guidance as well as its purchase price.

scenes.note: Illustrative installation only · Follow the exact appliance instructions

scenes.heading: Think beyond the lower sticker price

cues.text: A refrigerated portable air conditioner and an evaporative cooler are different purchases.
YourHome notes that portable air conditioners are less efficient than fixed split systems.
For frequent long-term cooling, our advice is to compare a complete fixed-system quote before choosing on price alone.

scenes.note: YourHome guidance + Smart Choice 365 editorial judgement

scenes.heading: 6. Compare complete installed quotes

cues.text: Ask for the exact indoor and outdoor model identifiers on the quote.
Check what pipework, electrical work, drainage and old-unit removal are included.
Then check written warranty and service terms, access requirements and exclusions. Supply-only and fully installed prices are different comparisons.

scenes.note: Our purchase checklist · Qualified installation and model-specific instructions

scenes.heading: Use your bill, not a headline tariff

cues.text: Use the usage rate on your own electricity bill. With time-of-use pricing, consider when cooling normally runs.
Label figures use standardised assumptions. Your weather, settings and home can change the actual bill.
Keep fixed daily supply charges separate from the extra electricity used by the appliance.

scenes.note: Energy.gov.au + Energy Rating methodology · Blank papers are illustrative

scenes.heading: Our verdict: buy for the whole cost

cues.text: Our verdict: get the room fit right, compare the same climate-zone energy figures, then add installation and running costs.
